plan.planning_summary: Refining route_01 (Ge/ZnS 20-layer two-cavity Fabry-Perot) based on prior iteration results showing 0.978 target score. Implementing feedback directive to replace uniform 500nm initialization with physics-informed quarter-wave targets computed as d_k = λ_center/(4*n_k). Three complementary routes explore 20, 22, and 24 layer counts while maintaining the verified Ge/ZnS material pair and two-cavity topology. All routes inherit parent_route_id = route_01 per refinement_chain requirement.

routes.title: Ge/ZnS Two-Cavity Fabry-Perot with Quarter-Wave Seeded Initialization (20 Layers)
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Physics-informed quarter-wave thickness initialization centered at λ=4.45μm (midpoint between CO and CO2 bands) will reduce search-space entropy and accelerate convergence toward resonant stacking conditions compared to uniform 500nm initialization, while maintaining the verified Ge/ZnS two-cavity topology.
routes.design_principle: Start from alternating quarter-wave layers (H=L=λ/4n) at band center, then apply computational optimization to adjust thicknesses for dual-bandpass profile with stopband blocking. Two Fabry-Perot cavities coupled in series shape the passband.
routes.proposed_topology: CaF2 substrate | [Ge/ZnS]_10 stack (20 finite layers) | Air superstrate. Explicit sequence: Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS
design_variables: 20 layer thicknesses with quarter-wave seeded bounds
soft_objectives: maximize transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm bands
minimize transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm bands
manufacturing_considerations: Ge and ZnS are conventional depositable IR dielectrics
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack resonance condition: d_k = λ_center/(4*n_k)
Fabry-Perot cavity transmittance maximum when (φ1+φ2-2δ)/2 = kπ
Higher index contrast (Ge/ZnS) reduces required film thickness and increases maximum transmittance
expected_advantages: Faster convergence due to physics-informed initialization
Maintains verified Ge/ZnS material performance from prior iteration
Quarter-wave seeding reduces risk of local minima far from resonant condition
known_risks: Quarter-wave at single center wavelength may not optimally serve dual-band requirement
20 layers may limit stopband depth compared to higher layer counts
Fabrication tolerances may cause measured transmittance to decrease relative to theoretical
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 20-layer Ge/ZnS multilayer filter on CaF2 substrate for dual-bandpass transmission. Initialize all layer thicknesses using quarter-wave formula d_k = 4450nm/(4*n_k) where n_Ge≈4.0 and n_ZnS≈2.2 at 4.45μm center wavelength, giving initial Ge thickness ≈278nm and ZnS thickness ≈506nm. Set optimization bounds to ±40% around quarter-wave values (Ge: 167-389nm, ZnS: 304-708nm). Wavelength bands: transmit 4150-4350nm and 4550-4750nm, block 3600-4000nm and 4850-5200nm. Normal incidence, unpolarized. Max 24 layers constraint satisfied with 20 layers. No metal layers. Use gradient_thickness optimizer with coherent TMM across all bands. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 3600-4000 nm, 4150-4350 nm, 4550-4750 nm, 4850-5200 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 um and 4.55-4.75 um bands; low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 um and 4.85-5.20 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high transmittance in stopbands; high reflectance in passbands. manufacturing constraints: no metal layers; maximum 24 layers; conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials.
routes.revision_reason: Implementing feedback directive to replace uniform 500nm initialization with physics-informed quarter-wave targets. Maintains verified Ge/ZnS 20-layer topology from route_01 which achieved 0.978 target score.

routes.title: Ge/ZnS Two-Cavity Fabry-Perot with Quarter-Wave Seeded Initialization (22 Layers)
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Increasing layer count from 20 to 22 while maintaining quarter-wave initialization will improve stopband blocking depth and passband flatness by adding one additional mirror pair per cavity, at the cost of increased total thickness and fabrication complexity.
routes.design_principle: Two-cavity Fabry-Perot with asymmetric mirror counts: input mirror (6 pairs), cavity spacer, center mirror (5 pairs), cavity spacer, output mirror (6 pairs) = 22 layers total. Quarter-wave initialization at 4.45μm center.
routes.proposed_topology: CaF2 substrate | Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS (22 finite layers) | Air superstrate
design_variables: 22 layer thicknesses with quarter-wave seeded bounds
soft_objectives: maximize transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm bands
minimize transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm bands with improved blocking depth
manufacturing_considerations: Ge and ZnS are conventional depositable IR dielectrics
increased layer count may amplify cumulative thickness tolerance errors
theory_basis: Bandwidth of BPF depends on number of layers - more layers enable narrower bandwidth
Additional mirror pairs increase reflector stopband depth
Quarter-wave stack resonance condition: d_k = λ_center/(4*n_k)
expected_advantages: Deeper stopband blocking due to additional mirror pairs
Better passband flatness from increased cavity coupling control
known_risks: Increased total thickness may amplify fabrication tolerance sensitivity
22 layers approach 24-layer limit leaving less margin for design adjustments
May not significantly improve dual-band separation if cavity coupling dominates

routes.title: Ge/ZnS Two-Cavity Fabry-Perot with Quarter-Wave Seeded Initialization (24 Layers)
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Maximizing layer count to 24 (full budget) with quarter-wave initialization will achieve deepest stopband blocking and best passband definition, representing the performance ceiling for Ge/ZnS two-cavity topology under the 24-layer constraint.
routes.design_principle: Two-cavity Fabry-Perot with symmetric high-count mirrors: input mirror (7 pairs), cavity spacer, center mirror (5 pairs), cavity spacer, output mirror (7 pairs) = 24 layers total. Quarter-wave initialization at 4.45μm center.
routes.proposed_topology: CaF2 substrate | Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS (24 finite layers) | Air superstrate
design_variables: 24 layer thicknesses with quarter-wave seeded bounds
soft_objectives: maximize transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm bands
minimize transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm bands with maximum achievable blocking
manufacturing_considerations: Ge and ZnS are conventional depositable IR dielectrics
highest fabrication complexity and cumulative tolerance sensitivity
theory_basis: The more thin-film layers there are, the narrower the bandwidth of the BPF
Maximum layer count provides performance ceiling for given material pair
Quarter-wave stack resonance condition: d_k = λ_center/(4*n_k)
expected_advantages: Deepest achievable stopband blocking for Ge/ZnS system
Establishes performance baseline for comparing reduced layer count designs
known_risks: Maximum fabrication complexity and tolerance sensitivity
Total film thickness may be large (reference shows 8.7μm for 24-layer MIR filter)
Diminishing returns beyond 20-22 layers for this spectral requirement
May exceed practical manufacturing tolerance budgets
